html:
SMTO-CMP-0044 — Required dependency activities have not completed successfully

GUID: ca259037-f9a6-443e-b3ec-f209dc50eaaf
Slug: completion-dependency-activities-pending
Domain: CMP · Subsystem: cmp

What happened

  • The task tried to finish, but a step that other steps rely on failed, was stopped, or hasn't finished. The answer so far and any successful results are kept.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look through the steps listed under this task for any marked failed, stopped, blocked, or still running. SMTO only counts the task as done when every step it relies on has finished successfully.
  2. Open that step and read its output to see why it didn't finish, for example a computer that couldn't be reached or a command that failed. The step's own output shows what has to change before it can succeed.
  3. Fix that cause, then ask SMTO in the conversation to finish only the steps that didn't succeed. Steps that already succeeded may have changed things, and running them again could repeat those changes.

What success looks like

  • Every step under the task shows as completed and the task finishes with its answer.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened in each step before asking again. Select Copy error details and send them, with the name of the failed step, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't rerun the whole request until you've checked which steps already made changes.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Required dependency activities have not completed successfully.

What this means

  • A dependency activity owned by this run fails dependency_satisfied under the current dependency policy. Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.

Why this can happen

  • A dependency activity owned by this run fails dependency_satisfied under the current dependency policy.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect policy, required/optional status and blocked reason; raw terminal state alone may not establish satisfaction.

How to fix it

  • Inspect each blocking activity_id, state and blocked_reason in the error's requirements (the run's dependency_activities). Complete, reconcile or deliberately cancel the unsatisfied nodes before completion; 'Require successful dependencies' in Agent Checks only relaxes confirmed failures, never cancelled, unknown or policy-rejected outcomes, and duplicate work must not be launched to pass the check.
  • Inspect the blocked dependency graph and reconcile or complete the required activities before claiming success.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect existing activities and their effects. Do not launch duplicate work to make the completion check pass.

How to verify the fix

  • The graph's actual satisfaction rules hold for current owned activities.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
